market_holds: Spot $48.12 at the 2026-11-09 close (sealed baseline). The stock was ~$70 on 2026-09-29, fell to $30.26 on 2026-09-30 when the Delaware court found the '327 PH-ILD claims valid and infringed, bottomed at $25.91 (10-06), and closed at $26.81 the day the UTHR settlement was announced (10-13). Since then it has climbed in a steady line: $33.94 on 10-14, ~$45 by late October, and $47.38 on 11-04 (+12.3% on the day UTHR reported and said existing YUTREPIA patients are not required to switch). Run-up is +73.9% over 20 days and +15.0% over 5 (Yahoo daily bars; baseline). The front-week straddle implies 11.8%, about 6.8% after removing ordinary volatility, but the ATM spread is 78% of mid, so that number is only indicative. Puts carry 15.6 vol points of skew over calls (downside is paid for). Prior bmo reactions: +25.6% (Q1, revenue beat), -10.5% (Q2), median |move| 3.5%. The quarter itself is already public: preliminary Q3 YUTREPIA net sales of $222.7m and cash of $396.1m were in the 2026-10-13 8-K. Published consensus is stale: Zacks Q3 revenue $187m and EPS $0.77 as of 10-28; another aggregator shows $218m. Q3 GAAP will probably carry the $380.7m settlement, so headline EPS will look like a large miss. The only guide on record is the pre-settlement 'clear line of sight to at least $1B net revenue in 2027'. Short interest was 17.3m shares on 10-15 (about 19% of the 89.5m shares out), up from 12.6m on 09-30 (Nasdaq). Analyst targets run from $33 (Wells Fargo, hold) to $70 (BTIG, buy, upgraded 10-14). The stock now trades on the post-settlement durability of YUTREPIA: how much of the base and the new-start flow was PH-ILD, and what Q4 and 2027 look like for PAH alone.
view: Nothing in this print is new about the quarter. Revenue and cash were pre-announced, and the settlement terms (stop promoting for PH-ILD, take it off the label, pay $380.7m in 2026-27) are public. The call is the first time management speaks on the line the stock now trades on: what YUTREPIA is worth without PH-ILD. Two public facts set that line. First, on the Q1 2026 call management said about half of YUTREPIA prescriptions were PH-ILD, so half of new-start flow is now lost to promotion and soon to the label. Second, on its Q3 call UTHR said existing patients are not required to switch and that little push to move them is expected, so the installed base runs off slowly instead of falling off a cliff. The stock re-rated on that second fact (+12% on 11-04), so it is in the price. From here management will almost certainly sound upbeat about PAH starts and cash rebuilding. It will also have to say something about the '$1B in 2027' line. That target was built on a launch half of whose new patients came from PH-ILD, so it is hard to keep, but Q3 annualises to $891m, so a reframed or softened number is possible without a disaster. Against that, a +79% recovery off the low, the last week's +15% and paid downside skew make a sell-the-news reaction to anything short of a confident reaffirmation slightly more likely. A ~19% short interest (stale, as of 10-15) and a cheap multiple (EV around $4.2bn against Q2 adjusted EBITDA of $96m a quarter) mean a confident October-trend disclosure could squeeze it just as hard. I cannot see which of these the release will deliver. No public script, claims or channel data on post-settlement YUTREPIA starts was findable. So the lean is slight and I make no call.

recommendation.reason: The reported quarter is already public. The deciding line is the post-settlement PAH-only outlook and whether the $1B 2027 target survives, and no public dated datapoint on October new starts exists for me to beat the price with. The main recent positive, that existing PH-ILD patients need not switch, is already tied to the +12% move on 11-04. Run-up and skew lean slightly down, short interest leans the other way, and neither reaches 65%.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A disclosure of October/November PAH new-patient starts at or above the Q3 pace, together with a reaffirmed at-least-$1B 2027 net revenue target (or a Q4 guide above ~$235m), would push the stock up hard into a crowded short. An explicit withdrawal of the $1B target with a flat-to-down Q4 would confirm the down lean.

questions_pursued.question: What did the settlement actually take away: new PH-ILD starts only, or existing patients too?

questions_pursued.answer: It bars marketing, promotion and the label claim. Nothing bars sales to existing patients. UTHR confirmed on its call that existing patients need not switch.

self_critique: The case for up is real. Management promised a 'broader update' on the call and has every reason to bring numbers showing PAH demand holding up. The PAS label change is not yet approved, so PH-ILD remains on label through at least part of Q4 and unpromoted prescribing may persist. EV/EBITDA is about 8x on a business growing 30% q/q, and 19% of the float was short as of mid-October. A confident reaffirmation of the $1B target could produce a +15-25% squeeze, like the Q1 print. The case for down is just as live: a withdrawn target, a PH-ILD share disclosed at ~50% of the patient base, or any sign of Q3 channel stocking ahead of a feared injunction, landing on a stock up 79% from its low. With no dated demand data I cannot pick between them, which is why there is no recommendation.
approach_notes: P4 ('priced in is a claim to prove') helped: the UTHR 'no forced switching' fact could be tied to the +12% move on 11-04 instead of being treated as new. P3's freshest-data search came up empty for a specialty drug with no public script trackers. Stakeholder routes (UTHR's call) were the only fresh source, and for that the playbook could say up front that payer/claims data is usually paywalled for rare-disease launches.
